tagline.text: Cagayan de Oro's August city fiesta honoring its patron saint

location.label: Location
location.text: Central Cagayan de Oro (around Gaston Park, Rio de Oro Boulevard and Duaw Park)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–2,000 (local transport and meals for 1–3 days of festival events; flights and lodging not included)

children.text: The Higalaay Festival is a month-long city fiesta that Cagayan de Oro holds around the August 28 feast of its patron saint, St. Augustine. The street dancing, civic-military parade, religious procession and river procession of the final week are the peak.

The Higalaay Festival is the annual city fiesta of Cagayan de Oro, the main city of Northern Mindanao, held in honor of its patron saint, St. Augustine, whose feast falls on August 28. "Higalaay" comes from the Cebuano word higala, meaning friend, and fits the city's nickname, the "City of Golden Friendship," so the festival is often called the "Friendship Festival." Until 2014 it was known as the Kagay-an Festival; in 2014 it became the Higalaay Kagay-an Festival, and today it is shortened to the Higalaay Festival. Both the old and new names are still in use, so it helps to search for both.

Its roots lie in a religious observance from the Spanish colonial period. The city's first Christian church, built near the fort by Fr. Pedro de Santa Barbara, is said to have been completed on August 28, 1780, the feast of St. Augustine, and residents have kept August 28 as the city's feast day ever since. A modest religious observance of the early 1900s has grown into today's month-long city festival, and August 28 is also commemorated as the city's day. The skeleton of the festival is unchanged: the final week is full of street dance contests and parades, and the feast day itself closes with a procession honoring the saint and a procession on the Cagayan River.

What makes this festival appealing is not one big day but the many smaller events spread through August. The 2026 program alone began on August 1 with the city agricultural fair Fiesta sa Kaumahan at Gaston Park and the culinary event Kumbira at the Limketkai Center atrium, followed by the official opening ceremony on Rio de Oro Boulevard on August 6. Food markets, a half marathon, a fashion event, the Miss Cagayan de Oro pageant and many sports tournaments followed, leading to street dancing on the 26th, the civic-military parade and marching band competition on the 27th, and the religious and river procession on the 28th. Even within the same August, what you see depends greatly on which week you visit.

One caution before you read on. The city tourism office announces the schedule anew each year, and the program changes. In 2026, for example, the city tourism office said it had dropped the float competition from the contest categories. The only practically fixed date is August 28; the two days before it are guessed from last year's pattern, so be sure to check the city's official announcements before you make plans.

Teams representing barangays (neighborhoods) march through the streets in colorful costumes and compete in dance, the biggest spectacle of the festival. In 2026 it took place on August 26 on a route that started at the Limketkai Center, ran along C.M. Recto Avenue and Velez Street, and ended at the Don Gregorio Pelaez Sports Center, with seven barangays taking part. It carried on through rain, so bring a raincoat.

blocks.title: Civic-military parade and marching band competition

children.text: On the 27th, a large parade and a marching band competition bring together schools, government offices and organizations. In 2026, 186 groups were reported as confirmed, down from 220 the year before. Floats from non-profit groups and sponsors could join the march without competing. Organizers said they were coordinating to finish the main parade before noon, so it pays to claim a spot early.

This is the centerpiece of the feast day on the 28th. A religious procession honoring St. Augustine takes place, followed by a river procession that starts at Puntod on Macajalar Bay and ends at Duaw Park near St. Augustine Cathedral. Rio de Oro Boulevard was recommended as a good place to watch. Watching from the riverbank is considered the highlight of the festival.

blocks.title: Kumbira culinary show and food markets

children.text: Kumbira is a three-day cooking competition with categories such as chef battles and dessert making, and is presented as the longest-running annual culinary show in the Philippines. In 2026, local specialties and snacks were sold on August 7–9 at the Higalaay Festival Market and the Kaon Ta Bai food fair. It is a good way to taste local food all in one place.

Right after the opening, the city agricultural fair Fiesta sa Kaumahan took place at Gaston Park. You can browse and buy locally grown crops, plants and processed goods, which makes it a good way to feel the city's atmosphere before the main parades. The program changes every year, so check the schedule.

blocks.title: Miss Cagayan de Oro and cultural shows

children.text: From mid-August the Miss Cagayan de Oro pageant takes place; in 2026 the 61st coronation night was held on August 22, and on the same day the musical Sayawit was staged at Rodelsa Hall. From August 7 an exhibit also ran at Xavier University's Museo de Oro. The fact that there is more to see than the parades is one of this festival's strengths.

Sports events ran through the month, including a half marathon (August 16), a national horse show, an Arnis Eskrima open, a swimming festival, a pickleball tournament and an esports league. Barangays and groups also hold motor rallies, charity fun runs, river boat races and the village feast Fiesta sa Barrio. Dates differ by event, so pick only the ones you care about and plan around them.

During the festival, a fireworks event hosted by a city shopping mall, the Higalaay Pyrolympics, has been held in past years. Whether it is held and on what date can change from year to year, so check city or organizer announcements before you go.

items.title: Peak 3-day route
items.subtitle: August 26–28: street dancing, parade and river procession

children.text: To watch the street dancing, find a spot at the starting point in front of the Limketkai Center or along C.M. Recto Avenue. In 2026 it took this route, but the route can change from year to year, so check the announcement the day before. Organizers aim to finish the main parade before noon, so arriving early is safer.
Around the Don Gregorio Pelaez Sports Center, where the parade ends, catch the awards and results, then have a late lunch at a restaurant in town. It gets very hot, so bring a hat and water.
Watch the civic-military parade and the marching band competition. With hundreds of groups taking part, the roadsides get crowded, so head out early and find a shaded spot.
Stroll slowly around Gaston Park and St. Augustine Cathedral and take in the downtown decorated for the feast.
Watch the faithful's procession around the church, where the feast-day Mass and religious procession take place. Check the diocese's announcement for the procession time.
Take a spot on the Rio de Oro Boulevard riverbank to see the river procession. It starts at Puntod and ends at Duaw Park. Confirm the exact start time locally.
August 28 is a fixed date, but the 26th and 27th can change from year to year. Before booking flights and a room, check the city's official schedule announcement.
Arrive in town early and take in the feast-day atmosphere around St. Augustine Cathedral and Gaston Park.
Eat local food at a downtown restaurant and rest. Restaurants are crowded on event days, so book ahead or eat early.
Watch the river procession from Rio de Oro Boulevard and catch the final scenes near Duaw Park.

The most common way to reach downtown Cagayan de Oro from Manila (NAIA) is a flight to Laguindingan Airport (CGY). Flight times and airlines vary by season, so check them on the airline booking screen.

items.title: Getting around town and entering downtown

children.text: In town you use jeepneys, the local city buses, and taxis. On event days some roads are blocked or controlled, so you may end up walking.

It is reported that since July 28, 2026, jeepneys and vans arriving from other areas may not enter downtown and must drop passengers at the Agora Terminal in the east or the Bulua Westbound Terminal in the west. This rule can change, so check the latest announcement.
Mobile signal has reportedly dropped near the parade routes, so agree on a meeting place and time in advance.

To see the festival properly, plan for the last week of August, especially August 26–28. Street dancing, the civic-military parade, and the religious and river procession are packed into these three days.
August is one of the rainiest months in Cagayan de Oro. The 2026 street dancing also went ahead in heavy rain, so plan for wet weather and bring a raincoat.

Rooms are hard to find and prices tend to rise in the final week of the festival. A room near the event areas, such as Gaston Park, Rio de Oro Boulevard and the Limketkai Center, lets you walk, but it can be inconvenient to get back when roads are jammed, so check the route from your lodging to the parade start in advance.

For food, the early-August food fairs and the Kumbira culinary event let you taste local specialties and snacks. Restaurants are crowded on festival days, so eat lunch early and pick up a simple snack near the parade. Choose places by local reputation.
Head out early in the morning to see the parades. It has been reported that organizers aim to finish the main parade before noon.
There is little shade, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water, plus a raincoat for wet weather. August is rainy.
There have been reports of weak mobile signal near the parade routes, so agree on a meeting place and time with your group in advance.
Drone filming requires prior registration. You are reportedly asked to register with the city's public information office and the police and be assigned a flying area. Do not fly without permission.
Contest categories and routes change every year. The float competition was dropped in 2026. Check the city tourism office's announcements before you leave.
Rules for entering downtown on event days may change. If you come overland from another area, find out first which terminal you must get off at.
Dress modestly near the church and the religious procession, and do not block the procession.
The only confirmed date is August 28, and the other event dates and routes are announced anew by the city each year, so be sure to check the latest announcement before you book.
In crowded parade areas, beware of pickpockets and wear your bag in front.
August is a rainy period, so the schedule may be delayed or changed.

This is the host city itself. Take in Gaston Park, St. Augustine Cathedral and the riverside promenade together.
